name: First Party Analytics
author: TMM Technology

sections.description:
Understand the visits behind your website decisions.

Which sources bring people to your site? What content do they explore? Are your pages fast and responsive on the devices they actually use?

First Party Analytics brings traffic, content and real-user performance reports into WordPress. Collect activity through your own website, store analytics in your site’s database and explore the built-in reports without needing a Google Analytics account.

Find useful answers in your analytics

  • Understand your audience. Explore traffic sources, referrers, countries, languages, browsers and devices.
  • See which content gets attention. Review page visits, sessions, visit times, on-site searches and visited links.
  • Prioritize performance work. Investigate real-user loading speed, responsiveness and visual stability with supported Web Vitals.
  • Put traffic in context. Distinguish human, user-directed AI, crawler, bot and unknown activity.
  • Keep reports close to your work. Open analytics in WordPress and view page-level statistics while editing content.

Discover how people find and explore your site

Use source and referrer reports to understand where visits come from. Explore popular pages, on-site searches and visited links to investigate what people want and which content they use.

For a publisher, that can inform the next article or a useful internal link. For a store, it can highlight product pages and search terms worth investigating. For a business website, it can help focus attention on the pages visitors actually reach.

Measure the experience your visitors receive

A speed test captures one set of conditions. First Party Analytics also measures supported performance signals from actual visits, giving you evidence from the browsers and devices using your site.

Reports include Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift where the browser and visit provide them. Use these signals to investigate slow loading, delayed interactions and unexpected layout movement.

Keep local reporting under your control

Raw analytics and processed reports are stored in your site’s database. External analytics sharing is a separate option, disabled by default; it is not required for the built-in reports.

Choose IP and cookie exclusions and use visit sampling to control collection volume. Accounts with site-administration permissions are excluded from normal tracking, while eligible logged-in customers can still be measured.

The plugin uses a first-party visitor cookie and can collect personal data. Review the Privacy and External Services sections when configuring your site’s notices and consent controls.

Understand the traffic behind the totals

A crawler is different from a shopper or reader. Traffic classification helps separate automated activity from human and user-directed AI visits, so request volume has more context. Classification is an estimate; it does not establish a visitor’s identity.

Investigate gaps instead of guessing

Administrative diagnostics show collection statistics, background parsing progress and stage timings when reports are delayed. Historical page-visit import tools support CSV and TSV data, including a GA4 import format; imported visits remain distinguishable from native collection.

Start with the included reports

The reports above are included in this plugin. First Party Analytics Premium is a separate add-on; detailed session traces and other Premium-only features are not part of this download.

Install First Party Analytics, review your tracking settings and make a test visit from an eligible browser session. Your first useful check is simple: confirm that the visit is collected and processed, then explore its page, source and available performance data.

Privacy

First Party Analytics uses visitor identifiers and records browsing activity. Depending on the request and enabled features, collected information can include visited URLs, searches, referrers, IP addresses, browser and device information, language, interaction events and performance measurements.

Raw analytics and processed reporting data are stored in your site’s database. Restrict access to analytics and exports, review data retention and describe the actual collection in your privacy notice. First-party storage alone does not establish compliance with privacy or cookie requirements.

Optional data sharing is disabled by default. Review the services below before enabling features that send information outside your website.

External Services

Country lookup database

When a MaxMind license key is configured, the plugin can download the GeoLite2 Country database from https://download.maxmind.com/. Download requests include the license key and database edition; MaxMind also receives the server’s connection information. Country lookups use the downloaded database locally rather than sending each visitor IP address to MaxMind.

Country reporting depends on an available geolocation database and is approximate. This product uses GeoLite data created by MaxMind, available from https://www.maxmind.com/.

MaxMind Privacy Policy | GeoLite License Agreement

Optional data sharing and recommendations

Enabling data sharing and recommendations connects the plugin to https://share.firstpartyanalytics.nl/. The plugin provisions a site token, sends analytics table exports in background batches and retrieves recommendations. Provisioning and delivery exchange site/callback information and authentication details as well as the selected analytics data.

This option is disabled by default and is not required for local reports. Review the data-sharing interface and the data to be exported before enabling it. Contact wp@tmm.ventures for service terms and privacy information.

Plugin notifications

The shared plugin library periodically requests administrative notices from https://wpplugins-midlayer.tmm-technology.com/. The request identifies the plugin and its version; the service also receives standard HTTP connection information, including the server’s public IP address. This notification request does not upload the local analytics tables.

Contact wp@tmm.ventures for questions about this service.

Optional external block-detection requests

Block detection uses the site’s own resources by default. If you select Google or a custom domain for block detection, visitors’ browsers request that external domain to test whether it is reachable. The receiving service can see connection information such as the visitor’s IP address and browser details.

Google modes use https://ads.google.com/ or https://www.google-analytics.com/. These are reachability checks, not a connection of the plugin’s reports to a Google Analytics account. For a custom domain, review the policy of its operator.

Google Privacy Policy | Google Terms of Service
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate First Party Analytics. PHP 8.1 or newer is required; test the configuration on staging before enabling collection on a live site.
  2. Open the plugin settings and review exclusions, sampling, script loading and optional data sharing.
  3. Configure your site’s privacy notice and any required consent controls before collecting visitor data.
  4. Visit a few pages in a separate anonymous browser session or with an eligible non-administrator account. Administrator visits are excluded.
  5. Allow background processing to run, then open the analytics reports in WordPress.
  6. Check the date range and explore Pages, Sources and Performance to see the available results.

If reports stay empty, check tracking exclusions, browser requests, consent and optimization settings, and scheduled background processing. Enable diagnostic submenus in Advanced settings to inspect collection and parsing.

Screenshots show example reports and an earlier interface. Data and available controls vary with your traffic, settings and plugin version.
sections.faq:
What does first-party analytics mean here?

The plugin collects activity through your website and stores its analytics in your site’s database. You can view built-in reports in WordPress without connecting a Google Analytics account.

First-party does not mean cookie-free, anonymous by default or free of all external requests. See Privacy and External Services below.

Which reports are included?

Reports cover general activity, visit times, interaction capabilities, sessions, pages, screen sizes, languages, countries, searches, visited links, user agents, referrers, traffic sources and performance.

Does it measure Web Vitals?

Yes. It collects supported browser performance measurements from real visits. Not every browser or visit provides every metric, and these reports are not a replacement for Google’s own Search Console data.

Why do my own visits not appear?

Users with site-administration permissions are excluded. Test with a separate anonymous session or an eligible non-administrator account, and check your exclusion and sampling settings.

Why are reports not updated immediately?

Collected events are processed into reports by background work. Processing delays, failed scheduled jobs, browser restrictions, exclusions or sampling can affect what appears. The Data Parsing diagnostics help distinguish collection problems from a processing backlog.

Will the numbers match Google Analytics?

Not necessarily. Different tools use different session definitions, exclusions, sampling and bot classification. Consent settings, browser blocking and collection methods can also produce different totals.

Does the plugin use cookies?

Yes. It uses a first-party visitor identifier cookie with a configured lifetime of one year. Browser settings and cookie deletion can shorten that lifetime. Review the collection behaviour and integrate any consent controls your site requires.

Will analytics add load to my website?

Yes. Collecting, storing and processing events uses browser, server and database resources. The impact depends on traffic volume and configuration. Use sampling and exclusions where appropriate, and monitor parsing diagnostics on busy sites.

Can I use it alongside other analytics tools?

Yes, but review the combined tracking and performance impact. First Party Analytics does not require Google Analytics for its built-in reports and does not promise identical measurements.

Is Premium required?

No. The built-in reports work without the separate Premium add-on. Advanced features provided by that add-on are outside this plugin’s included feature set.

Where can I get support?

Open a topic in the WordPress.org support forum or email wp@tmm.ventures.

Include the plugin and WordPress versions, the affected report and steps to reproduce the issue. Redact visitor identifiers, IP addresses, private URLs, credentials and other personal information before sharing diagnostics publicly.

1.2.58 2026-06-09

1.2.57 2026-06-08

Fixes

  • Data sharing: lower the default chunk size from ~90 MB to ~50 MB. A 90 MB chunk of a large, busy table (e.g. ~720k rows) could exceed the backend’s per-request processing budget and fail with a 502; ~50 MB roughly halves each request’s row count and insert time. Still overridable via the first_party_analytics_data_sharing_chunk_bytes filter — lower it further for very wide tables if needed.

1.2.56 2026-06-08

Enhancements

  • Data sharing: send each table in size-bounded chunks (~90 MB) via keyset pagination on id, so large tables stay under the upload gateway’s request-body and timeout limits. Each chunk is its own Action Scheduler task; a failed chunk can be resumed mid-table from the last confirmed-sent row without re-sending earlier chunks. Chunk size is overridable via the first_party_analytics_data_sharing_chunk_bytes filter.
  • Data sharing admin: show per-table chunk progress (chunks sent and the row-id cursor) in the batched-runs breakdown and the in-progress row.

Fixes

  • Data sharing: ensure tables larger than one chunk send all rows — previously a table could be marked complete after its first page, dropping the remaining rows.

1.2.53 2026-05-27

Fixes

When multiple URLs in the same import resolved to the same (post/term, day) — e.g. paginated archives, URL variants — extras were previously dropped by INSERT IGNORE and their visit counts lost.   • Understand your audience. Explore traffic sources, referrers, countries, languages, browsers and devices.
  • See which content gets attention. Review page visits, sessions, visit times, on-site searches and visited links.
  • Prioritize performance work. Investigate real-user loading speed, responsiveness and visual stability with supported Web Vitals.
  • Put traffic in context. Distinguish human, user-directed AI, crawler, bot and unknown activity.
  • Keep reports close to your work. Open analytics in WordPress and view page-level statistics while editing content.

Discover how people find and explore your site

Use source and referrer reports to understand where visits come from. Explore popular pages, on-site searches and visited links to investigate what people want and which content they use.

For a publisher, that can inform the next article or a useful internal link. For a store, it can highlight product pages and search terms worth investigating. For a business website, it can help focus attention on the pages visitors actually reach.

Measure the experience your visitors receive

A speed test captures one set of conditions. First Party Analytics also measures supported performance signals from actual visits, giving you evidence from the browsers and devices using your site.

Reports include Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift where the browser and visit provide them. Use these signals to investigate slow loading, delayed interactions and unexpected layout movement.

Keep local reporting under your control

Raw analytics and processed reports are stored in your site’s database. External analytics sharing is a separate option, disabled by default; it is not required for the built-in reports.

Choose IP and cookie exclusions and use visit sampling to control collection volume. Accounts with site-administration permissions are excluded from normal tracking, while eligible logged-in customers can still be measured.

The plugin uses a first-party visitor cookie and can collect personal data. Review the Privacy and External Services sections when configuring your site’s notices and consent controls.

Understand the traffic behind the totals

A crawler is different from a shopper or reader. Traffic classification helps separate automated activity from human and user-directed AI visits, so request volume has more context. Classification is an estimate; it does not establish a visitor’s identity.

Investigate gaps instead of guessing

Administrative diagnostics show collection statistics, background parsing progress and stage timings when reports are delayed. Historical page-visit import tools support CSV and TSV data, including a GA4 import format; imported visits remain distinguishable from native collection.

Start with the included reports

The reports above are included in this plugin. First Party Analytics Premium is a separate add-on; detailed session traces and other Premium-only features are not part of this download.

Install First Party Analytics, review your tracking settings and make a test visit from an eligible browser session. Your first useful check is simple: confirm that the visit is collected and processed, then explore its page, source and available performance data.

Privacy

First Party Analytics uses visitor identifiers and records browsing activity. Depending on the request and enabled features, collected information can include visited URLs, searches, referrers, IP addresses, browser and device information, language, interaction events and performance measurements.

Raw analytics and processed reporting data are stored in your site’s database. Restrict access to analytics and exports, review data retention and describe the actual collection in your privacy notice. First-party storage alone does not establish compliance with privacy or cookie requirements.

Optional data sharing is disabled by default. Review the services below before enabling features that send information outside your website.

External Services

Country lookup database

When a MaxMind license key is configured, the plugin can download the GeoLite2 Country database from https://download.maxmind.com/. Download requests include the license key and database edition; MaxMind also receives the server’s connection information. Country lookups use the downloaded database locally rather than sending each visitor IP address to MaxMind.

Country reporting depends on an available geolocation database and is approximate. This product uses GeoLite data created by MaxMind, available from https://www.maxmind.com/.

MaxMind Privacy Policy | GeoLite License Agreement

Optional data sharing and recommendations

Enabling data sharing and recommendations connects the plugin to https://share.firstpartyanalytics.nl/. The plugin provisions a site token, sends analytics table exports in background batches and retrieves recommendations. Provisioning and delivery exchange site/callback information and authentication details as well as the selected analytics data.

This option is disabled by default and is not required for local reports. Review the data-sharing interface and the data to be exported before enabling it. Contact wp@tmm.ventures for service terms and privacy information.

Plugin notifications

The shared plugin library periodically requests administrative notices from https://wpplugins-midlayer.tmm-technology.com/. The request identifies the plugin and its version; the service also receives standard HTTP connection information, including the server’s public IP address. This notification request does not upload the local analytics tables.

Contact wp@tmm.ventures for questions about this service.

Optional external block-detection requests

Block detection uses the site’s own resources by default. If you select Google or a custom domain for block detection, visitors’ browsers request that external domain to test whether it is reachable. The receiving service can see connection information such as the visitor’s IP address and browser details.

Google modes use https://ads.google.com/ or https://www.google-analytics.com/. These are reachability checks, not a connection of the plugin’s reports to a Google Analytics account. For a custom domain, review the policy of its operator.
